curriculumIdentifiers.role: everyday-property discussion; no tasting or direct contact in this product

learningOutcomeMap.description: Classify materials as acidic, basic, or neutral using observable evidence.
Use indicator observations to investigate the nature of selected samples.
Investigate an acid–base neutralisation demonstration and connect the idea to carefully selected everyday contexts.

concepts.description: Distinguish the three categories of aqueous samples using teacher-approved observable evidence.
concepts.safetyBoundary: Do not ask learners to taste or directly touch unknown substances. Use prepared samples and teacher-approved indicator procedures.

concepts.description: Explain how an indicator observation can provide evidence about the nature of a sample.
Interpret red- and blue-litmus observations from a controlled sample test.
Compare indicator evidence from teacher-prepared plant-based colour indicators.
Recognise that a teacher-supervised indicator investigation may use an observed change in odour as evidence.
concepts.safetyBoundary: No direct smelling of concentrated or unknown chemicals. Any classroom demonstration must follow the teacher's approved safety procedure.

concepts.description: Describe the evidence and purpose of a controlled demonstration involving an acidic and a basic sample.
concepts.safetyBoundary: Demonstration only with teacher-selected dilute materials and protective procedures; no learner mixing of household chemicals.

concepts.description: Relate the chapter's acid–base ideas to a real-life situation that has been checked by an educator.
concepts.reviewRequirement: Each example must be independently fact-checked and teacher-approved before it appears in questions or student explanations.
